proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mu_{p_0,A}\) denote the product \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\) law on the finite set \(\{0,1\}^A\), and define the bounded Borel function
\[
 \bar z(u_A)=\sum_{d_A\in\{0,1\}^A}
 z(u_A,d_A)\mu_{p_0,A}(\{d_A\}). \tag{3}
\]
The conditional design law is the fixed product law and does not depend on \(U\).  Consequently, the local-score representation and the defining property of conditional expectation give, for either wave,
\[
 m_v
 =\mathbb E[Z_v^{(w)}\mid\sigma(U)]
 =\bar z((U_{vx})_{x\in A}),
 \qquad |m_v|\le K_0. \tag{4}
\]
In particular, the same \(m_v\) applies to both waves.  Equation (4) also proves, rather than assumes, the required stationarity: for every \(t\in\Gamma\), the array \(((U_{tvx})_{x\in A})_{v\in\Gamma}\) has the same law as \(((U_{vx})_{x\in A})_{v\in\Gamma}\) because the innovation coordinates are iid, and the function \(\bar z\) is independent of \(v\).  Hence \((m_v)_{v\in\Gamma}\) is stationary under left translation and \(\mathbb E[m_v]=\tau\) for every \(v\).

The fixed conditional laws also imply independence of the primitive fields used below.  Indeed, for bounded cylinder functions \(f_0,f_1,f_2\) of \(U,D^{(1)},D^{(2)}\), respectively, conditional wave independence and the fixed product conditional laws yield
\[
 \mathbb E[f_0(U)f_1(D^{(1)})f_2(D^{(2)})]
 =\mathbb E[f_0(U)]
   \int f_1\,d\mu_{p_0}
   \int f_2\,d\mu_{p_0}. \tag{5}
\]
Thus the innovation coordinates, the first-wave assignment coordinates, and the second-wave assignment coordinates form three mutually independent product fields.  The extension from cylinder functions follows from the monotone-class theorem.

If \(vA\cap vgA\ne\varnothing\), then \(vx=vgy\) for some \(x,y\in A\), so \(g=xy^{-1}\in AA^{-1}=C\).  Therefore, when \(g\notin C\), the two innovation blocks in (4) are disjoint.  Independence of the iid innovations and centering of \(h_v=m_v-\tau\) then give
\[
 \mathbb E[h_vh_{vg}]=0\qquad(g\notin C). \tag{6}
\]
This derives the declared covariance support from the common footprint.  It also shows that \(C\) is symmetric and contains \(e\), as follows directly from \(C=AA^{-1}\) and \(e\in A\).

Given \(\sigma(U)\), the first score in a cross-wave product is a function only of \(D^{(1)}\), and the second is a function only of \(D^{(2)}\).  Conditional wave independence, boundedness of \(z\), and (4) therefore imply, for arbitrary \(u,v\in\Gamma\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_u^{(1)}Z_v^{(2)}\mid\sigma(U)]
 =\mathbb E[Z_u^{(1)}\mid\sigma(U)]
  \mathbb E[Z_v^{(2)}\mid\sigma(U)]
 =m_um_v. \tag{7}
\]
This proves the first asserted identity, including the case \(u=v\) and all overlapping within-wave footprints.

Stationarity and (7) imply, for every \(g\in C\) and every \(v\in J_g\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_v^{(1)}Z_{vg}^{(2)}]
 =\mathbb E[m_vm_{vg}]
 =\tau^2+\mathbb E[h_vh_{vg}]
 =\tau^2+\gamma(g). \tag{8}
\]
Here the last equality translates the pair \((v,vg)\) to \((e,g)\).  Hence averaging (8) over the nonempty set \(J_g\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[|J_g|^{-1}\sum_{v\in J_g}
 Z_v^{(1)}Z_{vg}^{(2)}\right]=\tau^2+\gamma(g). \tag{9}
\]
Let \(\overline m=N^{-1}\sum_{v\in I}m_v\).  Applying (7) term by term and using \(\mathbb E\overline m=\tau\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\overline Z^{(1)}\overline Z^{(2)}]
 =\mathbb E[\overline m^{,2}]
 =\tau^2+\operatorname{Var}(\overline m). \tag{10}
\]
Subtracting \(q\) copies of (10) from the sum of (9) over \(g\in C\) proves
\[
 \mathbb E[\widehat\Omega]
 =\sum_{g\in C}\gamma(g)-q\operatorname{Var}(\overline m)
 =\Omega-q\operatorname{Var}(\overline m). \tag{11}
\]

Since \(|m_v|\le K_0\) and \(|\tau|\le K_0\), one has \(|h_v|\le2K_0\).  For fixed \(u\), relation (6) leaves at most the \(q\) sites \(v=ug\), \(g\in C\), with a possibly nonzero covariance.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\overline m)
 =\frac1{N^2}\sum_{u,v\in I}\mathbb E[h_uh_v]
 \le\frac{Nq\,(2K_0)^2}{N^2}
 =\frac{4qK_0^2}{N}. \tag{12}
\]
Variance nonnegativity, (11), and (12) prove both inequalities in (1).

We next derive finite-sample concentration from the independent primitive coordinates in (5).  Put
\[
 T=\sum_{g\in C}|J_g|^{-1}\sum_{v\in J_g}
 Z_v^{(1)}Z_{vg}^{(2)},
 \qquad
 R=q\overline Z^{(1)}\overline Z^{(2)},
 \qquad
 c=\frac{aqK_0^2}{\nu}, \tag{13}
\]
so that \(\widehat\Omega=T-R\).  A fixed environment coordinate \(U_y\) belongs to at most \(a\) footprints \(vA\), because \(y=vx\) determines \(v=yx^{-1}\) for each \(x\in A\).  At a fixed \(g\), changing \(U_y\) can consequently change at most \(2a\) summands in \(T\), accounting for either endpoint.  Each product lies in \([-K_0^2,K_0^2]\), so
\[
 |\Delta_yT|
 \le\sum_{g\in C}\frac{2a(2K_0^2)}{|J_g|}
 \le\frac{4aqK_0^2}{\nu}=4c. \tag{14}
\]
The same coordinate changes at most \(a\) scores in each wave.  Thus each wave mean changes by at most \(2aK_0/N\), while both old and new wave means lie in \([-K_0,K_0]\).  The product identity \(x'y'-xy=(x'-x)y'+x(y'-y)\) gives
\[
 |\Delta_yR|
 \le q\left(\frac{2aK_0}{N}K_0
             +K_0\frac{2aK_0}{N}\right)
 =\frac{4aqK_0^2}{N}
 \le4c, \tag{15}
\]
where \(\nu\le N\) because every \(J_g\subseteq I\).  Hence one environment coordinate has oscillation at most \(8c\) for \(\widehat\Omega\).

A coordinate \(D_y^{(w)}\) in one assignment wave belongs to at most \(a\) local scores in that wave.  At each \(g\), it therefore changes at most \(a\) products, not \(2a\), because the other factor belongs to the conditionally independent wave.  Repeating (14)--(15) gives
\[
 |\Delta_yT|\le2c,
 \qquad
 |\Delta_yR|\le2c,
 \qquad
 |\Delta_y\widehat\Omega|\le4c. \tag{16}
\]
Every retained score uses only primitive coordinates in \(IA\subseteq\Lambda\); the same is true for both endpoints of every retained product because \(v,vg\in I\).  Thus \(\widehat\Omega\) is a Borel function of at most \(|\Lambda|\) innovation coordinates and at most \(|\Lambda|\) assignment coordinates in each wave.  By (5) these coordinates are independent, and (14)--(16) imply that the sum of their squared oscillation bounds is at most
\[
 |\Lambda|(8c)^2+2|\Lambda|(4c)^2
 =96|\Lambda|c^2. \tag{17}
\]
Apply the frozen McDiarmid bounded-differences lemma, first with all bounds multiplied by \(1+\eta\) and then let \(\eta\downarrow0\) to accommodate its strict oscillation convention.  For every \(t>0\),
\[
 \Pr\{|\widehat\Omega-\mathbb E\widehat\Omega|>t\}
 \le2\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{48|\Lambda|c^2}\right\}. \tag{18}
\]
Taking
\[
 t=\sqrt{48|\Lambda|}\,c\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)} \tag{19}
\]
makes the right side of (18) equal to \(\delta\).  The deterministic bias bound in (1), (18), (19), and the triangle inequality prove (2).

It remains to verify the F\o lner assertions.  Because \(e\in A\),
\[
 I=\Lambda\cap\bigcap_{x\in A}\Lambda x^{-1}.
\]
For a right F\o lner sequence and fixed finite \(A\), the union bound gives
\[
 \frac{|\Lambda_j\setminus I_j|}{|\Lambda_j|}
 \le\sum_{x\in A}
 \frac{|\Lambda_j\mathbin\triangle\Lambda_jx^{-1}|}{|\Lambda_j|}
 \longrightarrow0. \tag{20}
\]
Consequently \(N_j/|\Lambda_j|\to1\).  For fixed \(g\in C\), translation preserves cardinality and
\[
 |I_j\mathbin\triangle I_jg^{-1}|
 \le2|\Lambda_j\setminus I_j|
   +|\Lambda_j\mathbin\triangle\Lambda_jg^{-1}|. \tag{21}
\]
Since \(J_{j,g}=I_j\cap I_jg^{-1}\), equations (20)--(21) yield \(|J_{j,g}|/|\Lambda_j|\to1\).  The set \(C\) is finite, so taking the minimum gives \(\nu_j/|\Lambda_j|\to1\).  Substitution into (1)--(2), with fixed \(A\), \(a\), and \(q\), proves respectively the \(O(|\Lambda_j|^{-1})\) bias and \(O(\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/|\Lambda_j|})\) deviation radius.

As an exact smallest-instance stress test, take \(A=\{e\}\) and \(\Lambda=\{e\}\).  Then \(C=I=J_e=\{e\}\), \(N=\nu=a=q=1\), and the two terms defining \(\widehat\Omega\) cancel for every realized assignment, so \(\widehat\Omega=0\).  Meanwhile \(\Omega=\operatorname{Var}(m_e)\), and (11) reads exactly \(0=\Omega-\operatorname{Var}(m_e)\).  Thus the expectation identity survives enumeration of every assignment in the smallest finite volume.  The root-volume conclusion deliberately keeps \(A\) fixed and uses \(\nu_j/|\Lambda_j|\to1\); allowing the footprint to grow or the lag-pair interior to collapse would invalidate the final rate substitution and is not claimed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\Gamma\) be a countable finitely generated group with identity \(e\), equipped with a finite symmetric generating set and hence with its bounded-degree vertex-transitive Cayley graph.  Fix a finite set \(A\subset\Gamma\) with \(e\in A\), and declare the finite covariance-support set \(C=AA^{-1}\), with \(a=|A|\) and \(q=|C|\).  Let \(\Lambda\subset\Gamma\) be finite, put
\[
 I=\{v\in\Lambda:vA\subseteq\Lambda\},\qquad
 J_g=\{v\in I:vg\in I\},\qquad
 N=|I|,\qquad \nu=\min_{g\in C}|J_g|,
\]
and suppose \(N>0\) and \(\nu>0\).  Let \((U_v)_{v\in\Gamma}\) be iid with values in a Borel space \(\mathcal U\).  For \(t\in\Gamma\), use the left actions \((t\cdot u)_v=u_{t^{-1}v}\) and \((t\cdot d)_v=d_{t^{-1}v}\).  Conditional on \(\sigma(U)\), let \(D^{(1)}\) and \(D^{(2)}\) be independent, with the coordinates within each wave iid \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_0)\) for a fixed \(p_0\in(0,1)\).

Fix two exposure labels \(c_1,c_0\), a common no-carryover exposure map, and a common no-carryover potential-outcome schedule.  Require both maps to be \(\Gamma\)-equivariant: for all \(t,v\in\Gamma\), environments \(u\), and assignments \(d\),
\[
 E_{tv}(t\cdot d;t\cdot u)=E_v(d;u),
 \qquad
 Y_{tv}(t\cdot d;t\cdot u)=Y_v(d;u).
\]
For the known positive propensities
\[
 \pi_v(c)=\Pr\{E_v(D^{(w)};U)=c\mid\sigma(U)\}>0,
\]
define the exposure-IPW scores explicitly by
\[
 Z_v^{(w)}=Y_v(D^{(w)};U)
 \left\{\frac{\mathbf 1(E_v(D^{(w)};U)=c_1)}{\pi_v(c_1)}
 -\frac{\mathbf 1(E_v(D^{(w)};U)=c_0)}{\pi_v(c_0)}\right\}.
\]
Suppose there is one Borel map
\[
 z:\mathcal U^A\times\{0,1\}^A\longrightarrow[-K_0,K_0],
\]
independent of \(v\) and \(w\), such that, simultaneously for every \(v\in\Gamma\) and \(w\in\{1,2\}\),
\[
 Z_v^{(w)}
 =z\bigl((U_{vx})_{x\in A},(D_{vx}^{(w)})_{x\in A}\bigr)
 \qquad\text{almost surely},
\]
where \(K_0<\infty\).  Define
\[
 m_v=\mathbb E[Z_v^{(w)}\mid\sigma(U)],\quad
 \tau=\mathbb E[m_e],\quad h_v=m_v-\tau,\quad
 \gamma(g)=\mathbb E[h_eh_g],\quad
 \Omega=\sum_{g\in C}\gamma(g),
\]
and, under the common restriction coupling, define
\[
 \overline Z^{(w)}=\frac1N\sum_{v\in I}Z_v^{(w)},\qquad
 \widehat\Omega
 =\sum_{g\in C}\left\{
   \frac1{|J_g|}\sum_{v\in J_g}Z_v^{(1)}Z_{vg}^{(2)}
   -\overline Z^{(1)}\overline Z^{(2)}\right\}.
\]
Then, for every \(g\in C\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_v^{(1)}Z_{vg}^{(2)}\mid\sigma(U)]=m_vm_{vg},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E[\widehat\Omega]
 =\Omega-q\operatorname{Var}\!\left(N^{-1}\sum_{v\in I}m_v\right),
 \qquad
 0\le \Omega-\mathbb E[\widehat\Omega]
 \le \frac{4q^2K_0^2}{N}. \tag{1}
\]
For every \(\delta\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{
  |\widehat\Omega-\Omega|>
  \frac{4q^2K_0^2}{N}
  +\frac{\sqrt{48|\Lambda|}\,a qK_0^2}{\nu}
    \sqrt{\log(2/\delta)}
 \right\}\le\delta. \tag{2}
\]
If \((\Lambda_j)\) is a right F\o lner sequence, meaning \(|\Lambda_j\mathbin\triangle\Lambda_jg|/|\Lambda_j|\to0\) for every fixed \(g\in\Gamma\), and \(A\), hence \(C\), is fixed, then \(N_j/|\Lambda_j|\to1\), \(\nu_j/|\Lambda_j|\to1\), the bias in (1) is \(O(|\Lambda_j|^{-1})\), and the deviation radius in (2) is \(O(\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/|\Lambda_j|})\).  Thus the fixed-cutoff Palm population-variance diagnostic has root-volume concentration on every such amenable Cayley graph; no growing bandwidth or random graph distance is used.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former three score conditions did not require one site-independent local version and therefore did not by themselves imply stationarity of the conditional-mean field. The corrected hypothesis uses the directed common Borel local score map, while keeping the same group, fixed footprint, estimator, constants, and Følner conclusions; both the exposure map and the no-carryover potential-outcome schedule are now explicitly equivariant.

prose_updates.tldr: Two conditionally independent assignment waves on one no-carryover schedule identify the Palm population covariance through observable cross-wave IPW products. A joint assignment--innovation cylinder version, common to every assignment outside one null set, makes the local conditional score well defined; on a Cayley graph the corresponding single site-independent Borel score map yields stationarity and bounded primitive influence. These primitives give order-\(n^{-1}\) centering bias and root-\(n\) finite-sample concentration on F\o lner interiors, with the buffered integer interval giving the explicit size--power test and an exactly unbiased lag-separated version. A four-cell exact-local least-favorable schedule gives common support to the induced laws of the complete buffered graph--assignment--exposure--outcome record and proves a matching full-observation minimax lower bound. Thus, for distinct focal exposure labels, both the full-observation and score-vector separation radii are \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, and the one-wave interference papers study effect or estimator-variance inference. Viviano2020 already develops a two-wave network design in which a pilot estimates variance and the second wave optimizes participation and treatment; none of these works supplies a repeated-randomization test of the Palm population-covariance boundary or a full-observation minimax converse for it.
project_justification.niche: Conditional replication removes assignment noise from cross-wave IPW products. The joint assignment--innovation cylinder condition supplies one version simultaneously over all assignment cells; its Cayley-graph analogue is a single bounded Borel score rule shared by every site and wave. This common local rule derives stationarity and deterministic primitive influence on F\o lner interiors, while four local assignment cells leave unobserved schedule coordinates after two waves and give common support to the induced observed-data laws needed for a full-record information bound.
project_justification.fill: The project gives the cross-wave identity, order-\(n^{-1}\) centering control, root-\(n\) concentration, finite-sample size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated interval statistic under the corrected common local versions. For distinct focal exposure labels, it also constructs a causal-realizable four-cell submodel with \(\operatorname{KL}\le2N_ns^2\) and linearly changing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), proving matching \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) minimax rates for the complete declared observation and, as a corollary, for the score vector.

sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are applied to the same graph, exposure mapping, and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule after a prespecified washout; the deterministic covariance cutoff and analysis interior are fixed before assignment.
sampling_model.units: The canonical specialization observes \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzes its buffered interior \(I_n\). Exposure and outcome locality is a joint cylinder property: outside one law-null set independent of the assignment, one local Borel map represents every assignment cell. The group extension uses one site- and wave-independent Borel score map on a fixed right-translated footprint and deterministic F\o lner interiors of finitely generated amenable Cayley graphs.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments in each wave generate local exposure labels and realized outcomes under one common shift-equivariant schedule; the left shift acts on assignments and graph edges as explicitly declared in the corrected core. The full minimax observation contains the finite graph, both assignments, both exposure arrays, both realized-outcome arrays, and known propensity coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave, so every IPW division is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Propensities are known from the design. The mean-centered statistic estimates only the two wave means, the lag-separated statistic removes that centering bias exactly, and neither procedure estimates unit-specific conditional scores or fits a regression.

prose_updates.related_work: Janson2015 supplies the finite-dependent coboundary result used to interpret the zero boundary, but no two-wave statistic or testing experiment. Leung2022ANI supplies one-wave exposure-IPW and approximate-neighborhood-interference analysis; no ANI or graph-HAC transfer is used here. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings and known design propensities. Viviano2020 is the closest design comparator: it uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment for average treatment and spillover effects. The present work does not claim that two-wave network designs are new; it instead uses conditionally independent replications with common joint local versions to identify and test a Palm covariance boundary and proves a full-observation common-support minimax converse. LiWager2022 and FanLengWu2025 target causal-effect estimation and estimator variance under graphon models. Tsybakov2009 supplies the classical Pinsker and two-point testing inequalities used after the new four-cell likelihood calculation.
prose_updates.interpretation: The null \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) is a covariance-cancellation boundary, not a claim that conditional exposure effects are homogeneous. On the line, the corrected joint cylinder condition makes the conditional score a finite block factor, so Janson's result represents the null score as a finite-block coboundary. Rejection certifies positive Palm population variation; failure to reject only places that variation within the stated finite-sample threshold.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to one no-carryover schedule and one common joint assignment--innovation cylinder version. The full-observation converse includes the observed finite graph, assignments, exposures, realized outcomes, and known propensities, but not the innovations or unobserved assignment-cell outcomes. The graph extension requires a single bounded local score map shared by all sites and waves, a fixed footprint, and deterministic covariance-support sets on F\o lner interiors. No growing bandwidth, random shortest-path cutoff, approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT or Wald theorem, or BondEtAl2012 reanalysis is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal target is \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), the long-run covariance sum of fixed local conditional exposure-effect scores under the Palm law. The interval results and their finitely generated amenable Cayley-graph extension use a fixed deterministic local cutoff, bounded outcomes, overlap, two conditionally independent waves, a common assignment--innovation cylinder version, bounded primitive influence, bounded score dependency, and a common Palm mean. In the group extension, one site- and wave-independent Borel score rule is the primitive that derives stationarity. For distinct focal exposure labels, minimax sharpness holds for the explicitly encoded finite observed-data vector at \(p=1/2\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\); the score-vector theorem is a corollary. The note claims neither novelty of two-wave designs nor validity for richer observations that reveal innovations or unobserved potential outcomes.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem derives cross-wave identification, the finite-volume centering bias, and root-volume concentration from one common bounded local score rule, rather than assuming stationarity or a limit law.
statement_notes.gap: Existing interference results do not provide this fixed-footprint repeated-randomization Palm covariance diagnostic on deterministic F\o lner interiors.
statement_notes.consumer: The integer-line theorem is the specialization with \(A=\{-r,\ldots,r\}\); other finitely generated amenable Cayley graphs use the same explicit estimator and constants after replacing interval interiors by footprint interiors.
